verdict.root_cause: At 01:51:30 UTC platform-automation lowered recommendationservice's container memory limit to 32m (tr_40150e3a31bd). Recommendationservice's own request logs stop abruptly at exactly that timestamp with no shutdown, no traceback and no restart banner (tr_b3572e6653d8), and ten seconds later frontend begins emitting gRPC status 14 UNAVAILABLE with a 'no connection established' detail on its outbound client path, persisting through 01:57 (tr_59fbe80dca96). Traces confirm the failing edge is specifically frontend → RecommendationService/ListRecommendations: the client span carries the error and essentially all of the multi-second latency, no recommendationservice server span ever appears beneath it, and every other downstream edge (cart, productcatalog, ad, checkout and its whole subtree) is sub-10ms and error-free (tr_ee29b61ef6b7). The service's own error ratio stays flat at zero (tr_f2810da36fd8) precisely because it never gets far enough to return an error status — connections are not being accepted, so failures surface only at the caller, which is also why frontend's aggregate error ratio is partial (~22% peak) rather than total (tr_24d81b7acf89) and why no frontend change exists to blame (tr_98d97a1a8393). The mechanism in the world is that the recommendation container cannot operate within a 32MiB memory ceiling: it is being starved/killed for exceeding the limit rather than serving wrong values, so this is resource exhaustion that the limit edit initiated.
verdict.reasoning: Three independent signals converge on the same minute and the same edge. The change record places a memory-limit reduction at 01:51:30; the target service's log stream ends at 01:51:30 without any orderly shutdown; the caller starts failing at 01:51:40 with a connection-establishment error, not a deadline or application error. Traces localise the failure to a single edge and exonerate the frontend itself, the load generator, the unmeasured checkoutservice edge, and any broad backend slowdown — all other dependencies complete in milliseconds in the same window. The recommendation-side error ratio of zero is consistent with, not contradictory to, this picture: a process that cannot accept connections returns no error statuses of its own. I classify this as resource_exhaustion rather than bad_config because the wrong value is not itself breaking a request path — no address, credential or flag is pointing anywhere wrong — the container is failing because it cannot obtain the memory it needs to run under the new ceiling. The remediation is config_revert (restore the prior limit) rather than restart, because a restart under a 32m ceiling would reproduce the condition; the automation policy that emitted the edit must also be stopped from re-applying it.
open_questions: No direct kill evidence was retrieved: container OOM-kill events, restart counts, RSS/working-set metrics and replica readiness for recommendationservice were all explicitly not covered (tr_f2810da36fd8). The OOM mechanism is inferred from timing and log silence, not observed.

The recommendationservice log result kept only the newest 32 lines ending at 01:51:30; whether ERROR or memory-related lines were emitted after that point and dropped by truncation is not established (tr_b3572e6653d8).

The frontend log lines identify no target service, host or method, so the UNAVAILABLE errors are tied to recommendationservice only through the trace evidence, not through the logs themselves (tr_59fbe80dca96).
The change record shows no prior memory-limit value, so the size of the reduction and whether 32m was ever viable for this workload is unknown (tr_40150e3a31bd).
Which automation policy emitted the change, and whether it applied similar limit reductions to other services that have not yet manifested symptoms, is unidentified (tr_40150e3a31bd).

The change histories of frontend's other four dependencies (adservice, cartservice, checkoutservice, productcatalogservice) were never queried, and the frontend query covered only 15 minutes rather than the intended two-hour lookback (tr_98d97a1a8393).
Whether the condition self-resolved, was still ongoing after 01:57, or was masked by retries is not settled; frontend errors were still present at the last visible sample.
